title: Bukidnon Lumad’s fight for ancestral land remains uncertain
content:
Representatives of the Gulinsao and Maranding clans join a dialogue held at Provincial Tulugan Hall, Malaybalay City, Bukidnon, on September 7, 2026. Photo from Bukidnon Provincial IPMR Datu Makayuba Renato Sumbongan’s Facebook page

CAGAYAN DE ORO — After the fifth dialogue aiming to settle the land dispute between Indigenous peoples and a government agency in Barangay Dalwangan, Malaybalay City, Bukidnon, Lumad are still deprived of their ancestral land.

“They should return the land they borrowed,” Datu Aldren Gulinsao told Bulatlat in the vernacular following the dialogue last month.

Since 2017, the Gulinsao clan belonging to the Talaandig tribe has been reclaiming over 600 hectares of ancestral land, while their relative, the Maranding clan, has been claiming over 400 hectares. These form part of the more than 1,000 hectares of land under the title they obtained during the Philippine Commonwealth owned by their ancestor Maximo Gulinsao.

The Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR), on the other hand, said the subject land has been a titled property of the Department of Agriculture (DA) since the 1930s.

To assert their rights, in February, a few members of the Gulinsao clan forcibly entered the land, which resulted in the arrest of three individuals.

title: Festival-themed protest underscores teachers’ economic demands
content:
MANILA – On World Teachers’ Day, members of the Alliance of Concerned Teachers (ACT) held a protest near Malacañang Palace billed as “Pistang Protesta: Dagdag Sweldo, Hindi Dagdag Trabaho.”

Teachers from different public and private schools all over Metro Manila, as well as students and supporters marched Padre Noval Street corner España Boulevard toward Mendiola, October 5, 2026.

Carrying bunting flags and surrounded by ice cream carts, protesters called for a reduced and humane workload, allocation of six percent of GDP to education, P5,000 (approximately US$79.68) economic relief allowance and P50,000 (approximately US$796.81) entry-level salary for all teachers.

The current starting basic pay of a Teacher is pegged at P31,705 (approximately US$505.26) while the economic relief allowance is only P2,000 (approximately US$31.87)

Hogier Villarias, secretary general of Alliance of Concerned Teachers NCR, said that their call for salary hike is timely considering the increase in the country’s Gross Domestic Product.

“Our primary call remains a salary increase since our GDP grew by four percent, so we are expecting that wages should also be increased,” said Villarias, who joined the protest along with his fellow teachers from Andres Bonifacio Elementary School.

author: Josiah David Quising
title: Family, advocates remember 1987 killing of peasant leader, son
content:
Almost four decades later, they still remember. Friends and family held a memorial and candle lighting activity on October 3 to remember Valeriano Caro and his son who were killed 39 years ago by members of the Composite Reaction Force, a unit of the Regional Special Action Force, under the Cory Aquino administration.

Caro was a peasant leader from Kilusang Magbubukid ng Pilipinas (KMP) and chairperson of the Kahublagan sang Mangunguma sa Isla sang Panay (KAMIPA).

He and his son Rolito were killed in Barangay Galang, Oton, Iloilo on October 3, 1987. The memorial and candle-lighting were held on the roadside near the site where they were killed.

According to his wife in a report published by Amnesty International in 1988, Valeriano and her son were taken by the military at around 9:25 a.m. and were shot by a military officer just 70 meters from their own home.

On his 39th death anniversary, Valeriano’s family recalled his dedication to the plight of farmers in Panay.

“His legacy lives on in the continuing struggle to free farmers from landlessness, from bondage to the land, and from abuses at the hands of the regime,” Panay Alliance Karapatan said in a statement. (DAA)

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: ‘Army use of child a violation of int’l humanitarian law’
content:
MANILA – The Philippine Army’s publication of child pictures to pressure a New People’s Army (NPA) member to surrender is a violation of international humanitarian law (IHL), a human rights group said in a statement.

“Posting the child’s name, photograph and location while giving her mother an ultimatum to surrender was not only inhumane and exploitative, it was tantamount to holding the child hostage to compel her mother to do something against her will,” said human rights lawyer Maria Sol Taule, deputy secretary-general of Karapatan, in a statement on October 5.

In a deleted post, the 93rd Infantry Battalion of the Philippine Army published photos of a seven-year-old child with personal details under the pretext of a “birthday party” celebration to urge their NPA mother to surrender.

The Philippines is a signatory to the Geneva Conventions and is obligated to follow the rules of war under IHL. “Children shall be the object of special respect and shall be protected against any form of indecent assault. The Parties to the conflict shall provide them with the care and aid they require, whether because of their age or for any other reason,” the Fourth Geneva Convention stated.

title: Leyte farmer files harassment complaint vs military
content:
By Veronika Barbosa TACLOBAN CITY – A farmer filed a complaint on September 22 with the Commission on Human Rights Regional Office 8 against the Philippine Army’s 93rd Infantry Battalion (IB) due to intimidation against her and her family.

Accompanied by the National Union of People’s Lawyers Eastern Visayas and Katungod Sinirangan Bisayas, Brenda Lagado said that the first incident happened on July 28 in their house in Jaro, Leyte. “We were visited by elements of the Armed Forces of the Philippines. At first, they were just checking in on us but they eventually pressured us to confess that we have connections with the New People’s Army even if we have none.”

In the same month, Lagado said that her 16-year-old cousin was also interrogated by soldiers and alleged military assets.

“He [my cousin] was tending to farm animal when he was approached by seven soldiers and seven other individuals. At first, he was told to wait for a certain Basas who was supposed to talk to him but the latter did not arrive. He was instead confronted by a certain Simon who later grabbed him by the collar, hit him with a piece of chopped wood, and threatened that he will be hanged or electrocuted if he does not cooperate with them.”

Lagado said that his cousin was coerced by at least 14 men to divulge information about certain individuals that the victim does not know about.
